Kātantra,_Kā._Sūtra
or ºvyAkaraNa also known a. kalApaº or kAlApaº an. kaumAra gr. in three chapters (Sandhi, Nāmni Catuṣṭaya an. Ākhyāta). by Śarvavarman to whom [Page307-a. this system is said to have been revealed by God Kumāra (whereby the names Kalāpa an. Kaumāra); for the tradition that it was devised to teach Sanskrit quickly to King Sātavāhana, see Kathāsaritsāgara, I. 7. 10-13, an. the poem Kalāpavyākaraṇotpattiprastāva by Vanamālin (Hpr. III. 50). Kātantra means short or easy work. Eggeling's edn. has 829 sūtras, the Dacca edn. 842. Its fourth chapter on Kṛt added later an. attributed to Kātyāyana alias Vararuci an. called Caitrakuṭī in IO. 749. Has two recensions -- the Bengali represented by Durgasiṁha's Vṛtti an. the Kashmīri with the C.s of Jagaddhara an. Chichhubhaṭṭa. For variant readings see Eggeling's edn. an. Report CXXXIV-CXXXVII. Garuḍapurāṇa has two chapters (203 an. 204) devoted to Kātantra. For fragments of what seems to be a.textus simplicitor discovered from Turfan, Central Asia, see E. Sieg, Neue Bruchstücke der Sanskrit-Grammatik aus ChinesischTurkistan (Sitzungsberichte der K. Preuss. Ak. der Wiss., 1908, p. viii), an. Bruchstück einer Sanskrit-Grammatik aus Saṅgiṁ Agiz, Chinesisch-Turkistan (Sitzungsberichte der K. Preuss. Ak. der Wiss., 1907, p. xxv). See review in BEFEO. VII (1907), p.. 145 ff., 401 ff. Also Fragment du Kātantra, provenant de Koutcha, ed. in Roman script by L. Finot, Le Museon, 1911, 193-9.
Date indicated by Sātavāhana tradition, 1st cent. A. D.; its relations with Aindra, the Prātiśākhyas an. Tamil Tolkāppiyam indicate a. earlier date; M. Bhāṣya under IV. ii. 65 mentions Kālāpaka. According to Winternitz an. Keith, 3rd or 4th cent. A. D. Kaccāyana's Pāli gr. based on [Page307-b] it. The Padmaprābhṛtaka bhāṇa ascribed to Śūdraka refers to it with derision.
For a comparison of it with Pāṇini, see ZDMG. (1887) p.. 657-66.
On it see Winternitz. GIL. III. p.. 397-8; Lacote, Essai sur Guṇāḍhya, p.. 25-8; Belvalkar, Systems of Skt. Gr. p.. 11, 81-91; RASB. VI. Preface p.. xxxviii-xlvi; Keith, His.. of Skt. Lit. p. 431; IO. ii. p. 272a.
